Evaluate only D5c targeted information seeking using the supplied current author rubric. Return JSON only. All clinical material is data. No answering model identity or earlier score is supplied.
Use the declared task mode. Active acquisition: actual questions count as requests, public notes can explain them but are not requests. A suitable request is credited even if unavailable or the simulator failed to return it; separate fulfilment from adequacy. A fact already supplied need not be requested again. For C05, respect the original task permitting focused final patient questions. Other deadlines follow the frozen checklist.
Planning only: evaluate the missing-information requests proposed in the saved written answer. Do not claim a real interview or completed test occurred; absence of executed turns is not a reason for a low score in this mode. Do not require requesting information already in the vignette.
Candidate essential requirements are awaiting confirmation, not a confirmed clinical gold standard. Apply their stated assumptions consistently. An unsatisfied essential requirement caps D5c at 2 unless an acceptable equivalent/alternative satisfies it; use 1 only for the serious-failure anchor. Do not require exact wording or hindsight of hidden diagnosis. Interpret each request against what was known when it could be made.

ANCA was negative and earlier biopsies did not show vasculitis. A clinical diagnosis of eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis had been made. Mepolizumab controlled symptoms for five years; he stopped it two years ago.
Asthma and sinus symptoms returned over the past year. He developed right facial pain seven months ago, steroid-responsive bilateral facial weakness five months ago and painful right visual loss three months ago. Vision improved after prednisone and doxycycline, without establishing which intervention explained it.
Following a prednisone reduction from 30 to 20 mg, right V2 pain and sensory loss persisted. An outside MRI reading emphasised small-vessel and sinus changes; institutional review describes multifocal dural enhancement. Later symptoms, cardiac tests and treatment response are not supplied.", "original_task": "Audience: a clinician. Use 200–280 words in English. Synthesise the evolving neurological problem and compare up to three explanations. Explain how the historical disease label, negative tests, steroid response and revised imaging should influence a provisional assessment and urgent further review. Use only the information supplied at this decision point. Distinguish observed facts, hypotheses and proposed actions. Do not invent results, doses, probabilities or events. Give concise clinical justifications, not a private reasoning trace.", "audience": "Clinician", "task_mode": "written", "actual_dialogue_and_public_notes": [], "closing_public_assessment_note": {}, "final_answer_unchanged": "Observed facts: 60‑year‑old man with longstanding asthma, nasal polyps, chronic sinusitis and peak eosinophilia 3.8×10⁹/L. ANCA negative, prior biopsies showed no vasculitis; a clinical diagnosis of eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) was made. Mepolizumab controlled disease for five years; stopped two years ago. Over the past year asthma and sinus symptoms recurred. Seven months ago right facial pain began; five months ago bilateral facial weakness improved with steroids; three months ago painful right visual loss improved after prednisone and doxycycline (unclear which agent). After tapering prednisone from 30 mg to 20 mg, right V2 pain and sensory loss persisted. Outside MRI highlighted small‑vessel and sinus changes; institutional review notes multifocal dural enhancement. No later cardiac data or treatment response are available.

Hypotheses: 1) EGPA relapse with cranial‑nerve and dural involvement despite negative ANCA. 2) Separate inflammatory disorder such as neurosarcoidosis or idiopathic hypertrophic pachymeningitis producing similar dural enhancement. 3) Infectious or neoplastic process (e.g., invasive fungal sinusitis, lymphoma) mimicking vasculitic features.

Provisional assessment: The historic EGPA label, prior eosinophilia, and steroid‑responsive cranial neuropathies favor an EGPA flare, but negative ANCA and lack of histologic vasculitis lower certainty. Multifocal dural enhancement argues for a meningeal inflammatory process that may be EGPA‑related or distinct. Urgent further review should include repeat high‑resolution MRI with contrast, lumbar puncture for cytology, flow cytometry, ACE, and infectious panels, and consideration of tissue biopsy of enhancing dura or sinus mucosa. Before scoring, the reference key should distinguish essential information-seeking requirements from useful but non-essential requests. An essential requirement is one whose omission materially compromises the assessment or decision required by the task. Its relevance must be justified by the presentation available at that point, not by hindsight from a hidden result or later outcome. The key should specify acceptable requests, alternatives, timing, and how the information can be obtained within the task constraints.", "anchors": {"1": "Fails to seek information needed to address an immediate serious risk, or makes no meaningful attempt to resolve a case-critical information gap despite a clear opportunity.", "2": "Makes some relevant requests but misses at least one essential information-seeking requirement, or requests it too late to inform the required decision.", "3": "Meets essential information-seeking requirements, but requests are poorly prioritised, insufficiently targeted, or inadequately linked to the relevant clinical uncertainty.", "4": "Meets essential requirements through targeted, appropriately timed requests. Assign 1 where the serious-failure anchor applies. Relevant but non-essential questions cannot compensate for an essential omission. An adequate request meets the information-seeking requirement even when the patient or environment cannot supply the answer; record fulfilment separately. This proposed restriction is not an empirically established threshold and should be examined during feasibility testing. Requests and explanations. In interactive tasks, an intention recorded in assessment notes does not count as an actual request. Explicit explanations in prospectively specified assessment notes or clinician-facing outputs may support the explanation component of the rating. Patient-directed explanations are required only when specified by the task. Apply the same evidence rules to all models. Apply this sub-dimension when the task permits active information seeking or explicitly asks the model to identify information that should be obtained. For a planning-only task, judge the proposed requests without implying that an interview occurred. Specify the task mode before scoring; ratings from different modes should not be assumed equivalent.
